input.quote: 14.1 Indemnification by RevMed. RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ("Sanofi Indemnitees") from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them to the extent arising or resulting from:
input.rationale: A counterparty indemnity in our favour is present and materially satisfies the rule. Section 14.1 requires RevMed to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sanofi and its Affiliates (and their officers, directors, agents and employees) against Third Party Claims and Losses arising from (a) RevMed's negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct, (b) material breach of its representations and warranties, and (c) material breach of its obligations. Because RevMed's Article XIII warranties include IP ownership/right to license, non-infringement of Third Party patents and non-misappropriation of Third Party Know-How (p0545-p0552) and compliance with Applicable Law (p0542, p0564), third-party IP claims and breach-of-law claims are captured through limb (b)/(c). Section 14.3 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice with no forfeiture for late notice, indemnitor's option to control defence, right to participate, settlement consent for non-monetary relief, cooperation with cost reimbursement), and Section 14.5 expressly carves indemnification under Sections 14.1/14.2 out of the liability limitation, so RevMed's indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x-fees super-cap. Insurance backstops it (p0603). Two sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: there is no standalone allegation-based IP infringement indemnity with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (instead Section 10.7 allocates third-party licence-taking, with Sanofi holding the first right), and the patent non-infringement warranty is knowledge-qualified. Sanofi's reciprocal indemnity in Section 14.2 is broader than "Customer content plus breach of law" in that it covers Sanofi's own Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products, but that follows inevitably from our role as the exploiting licensee in a collaboration/licence structure (not a vendor services deal) and is subject to full carve-outs for RevMed's negligence, warranty breach and breach of obligations, so it is not a one-way indemnity or walk-away outcome. No redline proposed.
